sections.h2: Two county seats, one set of tax offices
sections.html:
Sebastian County has two seats, Fort Smith and Greenwood, and county offices, including the assessor's real estate line, are listed for both. The arrangement goes back to an 1860 compromise that split the county into two judicial districts. The 1874 Arkansas Constitution confirmed that the county may have two districts and two seats.

For a seller the result is simple: check which office location is closer, and phone first. The county had 127,799 residents in 2020, with a 2025 estimate of 130,641, and Fort Smith holds about 70 percent of them. It is the third most populous city in Arkansas, with 89,142 residents in 2020.

The county's reappraisal cycle ended in 2025 and runs five years, with Total Assessment Solutions Corp as the contractor. Appraisers visit to measure buildings and record condition. The county reviews sales from the final reappraisal year, keeps the typical market sales and uses them to value similar homes nearby. Values are set as of January 1.

The assessor is at 35 S. 6th, Room 104 in Fort Smith, phone 479-784-1516.

Your notice shows four figures, and knowing each one saves you a call.

  • Previous Value: the current full appraised value.
  • New Value: the full value on current market conditions.
  • Taxable Value: the figure used for next year's taxes, after caps and freezes.
  • Estimated Tax Change: the difference at the current millage rate.

Owners are mailed a notice only if the value went up. The county caps increases at 5 percent for an owner-occupied homestead and 10 percent for other property, as long as there is no new construction.

Start with an informal review. The owner carries the burden of proof, so gather sales of comparable nearby houses before you call. Check the assessor's data for errors such as wrong square footage, and ask for the comparable sales the assessor used.

Appraisers typically see only the exterior, so a cracked foundation or pest damage you can document may support a lower value. The Board of Equalization has nine members drawn from school districts, cities and towns, the County Judge and the Quorum Court.

Call the reappraisal firm at 479-424-2624 to start the informal review. For the petition and hearings, call the County Clerk at 479-782-5065.

People often skip the early steps and go straight to a hearing. The order below usually works better, and each step leaves a record you can use later.

  • Read the notice and match the four figures to your record.
  • Check the property data for wrong square footage, rooms or features.
  • Call the reappraisal firm to start the informal review, and ask for the comparable sales used on your house.
  • Photograph anything that lowers value, such as a cracked foundation or pest damage, since appraisers usually see only the outside.
  • If the informal review does not settle it, call the County Clerk about a petition and a Board of Equalization hearing.

Keep notes on every call: the date, who you spoke with and what was agreed. If you are selling soon, a corrected value also makes the property record look better to a buyer who reads it.

sections.h2: Liens, homestead credit and the senior freeze
sections.html:
City liens must be paid before or with taxes, so a lien on the property can surface at closing. Check for one early. The homestead credit application for the previous year is due October 15, and owners 65 or older, or disabled, can freeze value with proof of age or disability.

That freeze ends with your ownership, so a buyer starts from the current value. Personal and business property can be assessed from January 1 through May 31 without penalty. After that, the state adds a 10 percent penalty that cannot be removed.

A short folder speeds up every conversation with a title company or a buyer. Include the deed, your most recent tax statement and the assessment notice. Add permits for roof, foundation or addition work, repair invoices and photos of any damage you documented for the appeal.

If a city lien might exist, ask the city before you list. If you are an heir, bring proof of who inherited the house. Out-of-town owners can usually handle most steps by phone, mail and email, then sign at a title company close to where they live.

Having these ready also makes a cash offer easier to evaluate, since you can compare it with the real payoff rather than a guess.

Fort Smith has a humid subtropical climate and sits near Tornado Alley, so storm wind is a fair concern for roofs. The April 21, 1996 tornado killed four people and damaged much of downtown. An aging roof can complicate a retail sale because a buyer's inspector will check it, while a buyer paying cash can take the roof as is.

The Belle Grove Historic District is a 22 block downtown area with nearly 25 restored homes. If your house is near it or in another older neighborhood, ask the city what rules apply to exterior changes and repairs, and tell buyers what you find. A buyer or lender may ask about the age of the house, past repairs and any exterior work, so keep invoices and permits handy. Roads such as Interstates 40, 49 and 540 and U.S. 64, 71 and 271 make commute distance an easy selling point.

Ask the county for the balance on the parcel and let the title company pay it from your proceeds. Settle any city lien in the same step, since a lien must be paid before or with the taxes. Then the deed is recorded and the new owner starts from the current value.

A cash sale skips the lender's appraisal and any repair demands. It does not skip the tax payoff, so compare any offer with your balance to find your net. Ask for the offer in writing, confirm the closing date and ask who pays the recording and transfer costs before you agree.

After you accept an offer, a title company searches the record for taxes, liens and other recorded problems. Bring your last tax statement and the deed, along with any notice from the assessor. If you have owner-occupied homestead status, note that it ends with the sale.

At closing you sign the deed and the title company pays off what is owed from the proceeds, records the deed and gives you the remaining balance. Review the settlement statement a day early if you can, and ask questions about any line you do not recognize. With a cash buyer and a clean search, you can choose the closing date.

faqs.q: Why does Sebastian County have two county seats?
faqs.a: An 1860 compromise created two judicial districts, and the 1874 Arkansas Constitution confirmed two seats, Fort Smith and Greenwood.

faqs.q: When did Sebastian County last reappraise?
faqs.a: The cycle ended in 2025. It runs five years and is handled by Total Assessment Solutions Corp across 56,876 parcels.

faqs.q: Do Sebastian County owners get a notice if their value drops?
faqs.a: No. The assessor mails a notice only when a property's value increases.

faqs.q: How much can my Sebastian County assessment rise in a year?
faqs.a: By up to 5 percent for an owner-occupied homestead and up to 10 percent for other property, as long as there is no new construction.

faqs.q: Can a buyer keep my senior tax freeze?
faqs.a: No. The freeze does not transfer when the property is sold.
